text: Maria shared use of the Rakuyo weapon with her companion Simon.
The Burial Blade was forged from caryll runes-adjacent ciderite (a metal that falls from the heavens) and was designed not for combat but for a funeral rite, a dirge of farewell.
The hunter's default starting equipment, the Saw Cleaver and Hunter Pistol, was chosen to represent a balanced, versatile kit suitable for varied play styles.

Ludwig's Holy Blade was designed with an elongated transforming form evoking both religious ceremonial swords and monstrous proportions, transforming from a standard sword into an enormous greatsword that echoes the proportions of the beast Ludwig became, mirroring his own tragic transformation.
The Saw Cleaver transforms between a compact single-handed form and an extended serrated form, reflecting both surgical medicine and improvised butchery.
The Threaded Cane transforms into a flexible whip-like weapon, offering a distinctly different combat rhythm from the Saw Cleaver.
The Kirkhammer combines a smaller sword form with a massive stone hammer form, offering contrast between fast strikes and slow devastating blows.
The Chikage allows players to intentionally corrupt the blade with blood for increased damage, reinforcing the game's theme of power at self-inflicted cost.
The Beast Cutter transforms into a two-handed dual-blade configuration and synergizes with/punishes the hunter's temporary beast transformation from Beast Blood Pellets.
Firearms like the Hunter Pistol and Hunter Blunderbuss were balanced primarily as parrying and stagger tools rather than significant damage sources.
The Evelyn hand cannon was designed with unusually high damage output at the cost of significant stamina consumption, offering a firearms-focused build path.
The Rakuyo and Holy Moonlight Sword are late-game and DLC weapons tied mechanically and narratively to specific late-game locations and characters.
The Whirligig Saw functions as a spinning mechanical blade associated with a particular boss encounter's combat style.
The Boom Hammer incorporates an explosive mechanism directly into its melee attacks, an unusual design even among Bloodborne's varied weapons.

Rare hidden weapons like Simon's Bowblade require completing specific, easily missed sequences of events to acquire, and carry narrative significance connected to specific NPCs and storylines beyond their combat stats.
The Tonitrus, an electrically charged hammer, includes a charging mechanic that boosts damage output at the cost of the player's own health.
The Hunter Axe transforms into an elongated polearm form and was designed as an accessible introduction to the trick weapon mechanic for new players.

Ludwig's Holy Blade and the Rakuyo, both introduced in The Old Hunters expansion, remain among the most popular and frequently used weapons in Bloodborne's player community even years after the expansion's release.
Lady Maria's weapon, the Rakuyo, is a dual blade trick weapon inspired by traditional Japanese sword pairing conventions, distinguishing it from the base game's mostly European-inspired weapons.
Weapon designs like whip swords and cane swords in Bloodborne were inspired by real historical concealed weapons used by wealthy and aristocratic Europeans.
Real historical medical instruments like surgical saws and bleeding equipment served as direct visual references for many Bloodborne weapon designs.
Some rare weapon variants require players to defeat specific bosses without using certain consumable items, adding tension between survival and reward collection.
The Hunter Blunderbuss was designed with a wider damage spread compared to the more precise Hunter Pistol.
Several rare and unique firearms tied to specific NPCs and quest lines offer unconventional mechanical effects distinct from standard firearms.
The Repeating Pistol offers sustained ranged damage output at the cost of the precise single-shot parry timing of standard firearms.
